Class ContainerElement<T extends ContainerElement<T>>

java.lang.Object
dev.tamboui.toolkit.element.StyledElement<T>
dev.tamboui.toolkit.element.ContainerElement<T>
Type Parameters:
T - the concrete container type for method chaining
All Implemented Interfaces:
Styleable, Element
Direct Known Subclasses:
Column, ColumnsElement, DialogElement, FlowElement, GridElement, InlineScopeElement, Panel, Row, ScrollableElement, StackElement
public abstract class ContainerElement<T extends ContainerElement<T>> extends StyledElement<T>
Base class for container elements that hold children and forward events to them.

When a container receives an event it doesn't handle itself, it forwards the event to its children. This enables interactive elements (lists, text inputs) inside containers to receive events when their parent container is focused.

Subclasses should:

  • Use children to store child elements
  • Override StyledElement.renderContent(Frame, Rect, RenderContext) for layout-specific rendering

    • handleKeyEvent

      public EventResult handleKeyEvent(KeyEvent event, boolean focused)
      Handles key events by first trying custom handlers, then forwarding to children.

      Children receive events with focused=true since they are within the focused container's subtree.

      Specified by:
      handleKeyEvent in interface Element
      Overrides:

      Returns:

    • handleMouseEvent

      public EventResult handleMouseEvent(MouseEvent event)
      Handles mouse events by first trying custom handlers, then forwarding to children.

      Only forwards to children whose rendered area contains the mouse position, ensuring that mouse events are routed to the correct child in multi-panel layouts.

      Specified by:
      handleMouseEvent in interface Element
      Overrides:
      handleMouseEvent in class StyledElement<T extends ContainerElement<T>>
      Parameters:
      event - the mouse event
      Returns:
      HANDLED if this container or a child handled the event
